question: Two busway tie sections are fed from separate sources. ATS 7.4 requires a phasing test, and it must be done:
choices: From a temporary generator before the permanent sources are connected
From the permanent sources that will feed them
With a phase-rotation meter on de-energized bus
Only if the busway is rated above 1000 V
explanation: The purpose is to prove the real sources line up in phase across the tie. A temporary source can't prove that, so ATS says the test must come from the permanent sources. Source: ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 7.4.B.5 and D.5.

question: A 4.76 kV nonsegregated-phase bus run gets a field withstand test, and the manufacturer is silent. The maximum ac value in ATS Table 100.17 is:
choices: 20 kV
explanation: Table 100.17 gives 14.2 kV ac for 4.76 kV nonsegregated bus. 27.0 kV is the 8.25 kV and 15.0 kV row. That table has no dc value for this class, and ATS says to use the ac value where no dc value is shown. Source: ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 7.4.B.3 and Table 100.17.

question: How is the dielectric withstand applied to a metal-enclosed busway under ATS 7.4?
choices: All three phases tied together and tested to ground in one shot
Phase-to-phase only, with ground floating
Phase-to-neutral, with the enclosure isolated
Phase-to-ground, with the phases not under test grounded
explanation: Each phase is tested to ground with the other phases grounded. Values come from the manufacturer or Table 100.17. Source: ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 7.4.B.3.

question: On outdoor rigid bus rated 34.5 kV (nominal), the manufacturer gives no withstand value. ATS 7.21 uses Table 100.19, which gives a maximum ac test of:
explanation: Table 100.19 lists 42.0 kV ac and 59.4 kV dc for the 34.5 kV class, applied for one minute. 30.0 kV is the 25 kV class and 57.0 kV is the 46 kV class. Source: ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 7.21.B.3 and Table 100.19.

question: Which inspection item is specific to outdoor bus structures in ATS 7.21?
choices: Support insulators are clean and undamaged
Weep-hole plugs are installed per the manufacturer
Busway joint shields are in place
Space heaters are energized
explanation: Outdoor bus is carried on station post insulators, so ATS checks that they are clean and intact. Weep-hole plugs, joint shields, and heaters belong to metal-enclosed busway under ATS 7.4. Source: ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 7.21.A.4.

question: How does ATS 7.21 set up the insulation-resistance test on outdoor bus rated below 46 kV?
choices: All phases tied together and measured to ground in one reading
Phase-to-phase only, with ground lifted
Each phase to ground, with the other phases grounded
Across each support insulator individually
explanation: Each bus phase is measured to ground with the other phases grounded. The voltage comes from the manufacturer or Table 100.1. The step is written for equipment rated below 46 kV. Source: ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 7.21.B.2.

question: A 350 ft low-voltage busway run reads 0.25 MΩ phase-to-ground, and the manufacturer gives no minimum. Under ATS 7.4:
choices: Accept, because 0.25 MΩ exceeds 100 kΩ
Investigate; the minimum is about 0.29 MΩ
Accept, because long runs have no minimum
Proceed to the withstand test to see whether the insulation holds
explanation: Minimum MΩ = 100 / length in feet = 100 / 350 = 0.286 MΩ. The reading is below that, so investigate. ATS says not to proceed with the dielectric withstand until insulation resistance is raised above minimum. Source: ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 7.4.D.2.a.

question: A 69 kV outdoor bus structure is being accepted with no manufacturer data. Which statement matches ATS 7.21?
choices: Insulation resistance at 5 kV is required first, then a 160 kV ac withstand for 1 minute
Withstand up to 84 kV ac for 1 minute; the IR step covers only below 46 kV
No dielectric test applies above 46 kV
Withstand at 118.8 kV ac for 15 minutes
explanation: Table 100.19 gives 84.0 kV ac (118.8 kV dc) for the 69 kV class, for one minute. The 7.21 insulation-resistance step names equipment below 46 kV. Power factor is optional. Source: ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 7.21.B.2, B.3, B.4 and Table 100.19.
reference: ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 7.21.B.2, B.3, B.4 and Table 100.19

question: You have only a dc hipot, and Table 100.17 shows no dc value for 15 kV nonsegregated bus. ATS 7.4 says:
choices: Use 1.414 times the ac value as dc
Skip the withstand and rely on megger readings
Use the 37.5 kV dc value borrowed from the switchgear table, Table 100.2
Use the ac value, so the withstand is done at 27 kV ac
explanation: Where Table 100.17 shows no dc value, ATS says an ac value is to be used. Its note also says the dc column, where it exists, doesn't create a requirement for dc testing. Source: ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 7.4.B.3 and Table 100.17 note 2.
